task_title: Idea Chat script generation drops with "lost connection, please refresh" mid-run (Ben, 2026-09-04 ~00:20Z) — root-cause the generation timeout and make refresh resume instead of restart
close_reason:
ROOT CAUSE (AC1): the browser aborted, not the backend. apps/frontend/app/src/stores/auth-api.ts:601 applies API_TIMEOUTS.STANDARD (120000 ms in production) to every request without an explicit timeout, and useIdeaChat never set one on /generate or /refine. The Vercel function behind them is entitled to 800 s (apps/backend/vercel.json maxDuration), had already taken the iterate credit, and went on to finish and commit the work. The ofetch TimeoutError becomes statusCode 0, which friendly-error-message.ts:16 maps to errors.networkGeneric = "Failed to load. Please refresh or check your connection and try again." (locales/en.json:9950) — the literal message Ben reported, and the prod frontend cluster "Network Error Detected … timeout: 120000" (212 hits / 116 users / 30 d). Vercel runtime LOGS for 2026-09-04 were past retention (400 ExceedsBillingLimitError), so the proof is the code path plus the 7-day error clusters plus a live staging reproduction rather than the original request's log line; stated plainly rather than implied.

A second defect surfaced during the work and was not in the brief: IdeaChatPanel.vue onMounted treats a phase with zero turns as fresh work and auto-fires generatePhase. After a mid-run refresh that starts a SECOND generation on top of the still-running first — the "it started over" half of the report (Jess Webber, 2026-08-14). Fixed here too.

FIX (AC2), three parts: (1) /generate and /refine now use API_TIMEOUTS.LONG_RUNNING (300 s), the tier that file already documents for multi-step LLM pipelines, well under the 800 s ceiling. (2) New session field pendingGeneration {phase, kind, startedAt}, published before the model work and cleared when it settles — including a clear-and-persist on model failure so a dead run never blocks a retry — and suppressed on read past PENDING_GENERATION_STALE_MS (860 s = ceiling + slack) so a teardown corpse cannot strand anyone. "Zero turns" no longer means "nothing happened". (3) An interrupted request re-reads /session instead of dead-ending: recovered work appears with no error at all; work still running gets copy saying it is saved and will not be re-charged; mount waits for a live run rather than starting a second one. A follow-up commit split the resume outcome into 'recovered' | 'pending' | 'unreachable' so an offline creator is not told their script is still being written — a boolean had collapsed "did not find it" with "never reached the server". Credits were already idempotent on (workspaceUid,'iterate',itemId); the client now stops pre-flighting a paywall against a session the server already charged. auth-api additionally tags the manufactured network error timedOut and logs the request's REAL timeout instead of hardcoding STANDARD — that log line is the telemetry this was diagnosed from and it was misreporting custom-timeout calls.

TESTS (AC3), both shown RED before the fix: apps/frontend/app/src/composables/__tests__/useIdeaChat.interrupted-generation.test.ts (8 tests; 6 of 7 failed pre-fix, the 7th being a deliberate guard that a real 400 still errors) and apps/backend/src/items/idea-chat/idea-chat.service.pending-generation.spec.ts (9 tests, 9/9 failed pre-fix).

GATES: backend jest src/items/idea-chat 67 suites / 996 tests pass; frontend vitest 35 files / 400 tests pass; nuxt typecheck exit 0 with 0 errors; backend tsc --noEmit 36 errors byte-identical to the stashed baseline (pre-existing missing optional deps in src/mcp and src/oauth, no regression); eslint 0 errors on every touched file.

EVIDENCE (AC4) — before/after on deployed staging, same unedited instrument, same workspace, same phase, four artifacts under artifacts_root/cas-a6f7/ (before/after PNG + before/after trace JSON). Deployment ids: frontend dpl_Czizm7gdmRWDiJg96nQPrWxiq3Nv and backend dpl_775LJWyG6xs4y366fEv3ofggS2ku, both sha 986efe218 (PR #2177); frontend alias list checked directly to confirm staging.gabber.studio serves that build; Actions run 34248104221 success. BEFORE (15:49:07Z): upstream 200, server committed 1 assistant turn with 3 framework options, UI showed an EMPTY Framework step under "Failed to load. Please refresh…", session.pendingGeneration key absent. AFTER (16:08:04Z): upstream 200, same 1 turn / 3 options committed, all three cards RENDERED on screen with rationales and citations, NO banner at all (bannerVisible false), pendingGeneration key present with value null. The key going from absent to present-but-null is itself the control proving the new backend served the after run, not a frontend-only effect. The instrument cannot observe the marker mid-run (it awaits the real upstream response before dropping it), so that half is proven instead by the backend spec reading the persisted document while the model mock runs; the supervisor amended the close condition to exactly this split and directed no spec edit and no third capture.

Two process points worth recording: the FIRST before-capture was rejected and re-run because its generate returned 402 INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS — the abort had dropped a request the server already refused, so the artifact would have shown the correct banner while never testing the resume claim it existed to support. Root cause (corrected from the finding): not the slot-map guards — voice-restyle-baseline.ts rebuilds the reassembled document 1:1 so those cannot fire. Two per-slot prose guards were counting rather than checking. Pass 1 (PR #2335): STRUCTURAL_DELIMITER required an EQUAL sentence count and CONTENT_PRESERVATION failed on newNouns/nounCountGrew, so a voice could not even insert the signature phrase the product asks the user to declare. LOCKED_FACT anchors, proper nouns, polarity, CTA and all SLOT_* guards untouched. Layout-bound media unaffected, pinned by test. task_title: Dropbox: support team/business namespace so users can browse their business Dropbox
close_reason:
Delivered and merged. PR #932 merged into the epic branch as 5ede500f at 04:23:10Z; head 9690fd21 is an ancestor of the epic tip and the branch content is identical to it.

Dropbox team/business namespace support is complete and shipped across PRs #905, #913, #918, #924, #927, #930 (-> 8f3bfae9), #931 (-> 80975b5a) and #932 (-> 5ede500f). The customer-reported problem is addressed: namespace ids are persisted on connect from usersGetCurrentAccount root_info, the Dropbox client sets pathRoot for team accounts, list/import/download thread the selected namespace, and the picker exposes the Personal/Team switch only when the account has a distinct root namespace.

Exit criterion met: Copilot review 5205460697 on exact head 9690fd21 reported 0 inline and 0 suppressed comments, and the final CI run was green on every gate.

macOS proof is recorded in the platform_proof note (Darwin 25.6.0 arm64, Node v22.18.0): the scoped Dropbox/items/projects/lib suites pass 298/298, and the production typecheck exits 0. The full backend suite is 2224 passed / 17 failed, where the 17 are the pre-existing failures in workspace-roles.service, users.controller and firebase-auth.strategy; none of those files is in this diff and the identical 17 fail on base 80975b5a. Debt-aware gates versus that base: ESLint 476 -> 476 and tsc 49 -> 49, zero added diagnostics on both.

Defects found and fixed during the convergence loop, several of them regressions introduced by my own earlier rounds: the connection fence compared a project identity against a workspace row, which would have rejected every legacy project-level webhook import; dropboxPath was accepted from the public attachment DTO and treated as proof of Dropbox provenance, letting any workspace writer block an administrator's namespace change with a 409; a stale pre-transaction snapshot allowed dropbox_namespace to be written with no lock and none of the invariant checks; job folder matching used a raw prefix so a job configured for /photos also captured /photos2; orphan cleanup reused the already-exhausted delivery deadline and therefore aborted immediately; a deadline-bounded token refresh reported a transient timeout to users as invalid credentials; and a throwing finally block replaced the typed fence error with a generic one.

Documented residual, agreed with the supervisor as outside the zero-findings bar: a client-side PutObject abort can let S3 land the object after the best-effort delete has been processed, stranding an unreferenced key. Its cost is storage, not a broken attachment. It is marked in code as KNOWN RESIDUAL WINDOW and tracked as cas-790b (P3) with the exact call site, reproduction ordering and proposed design.

The team_data.member OAuth scope is being removed separately as cas-feee on another worker; this branch never modified DROPBOX_OAUTH_SCOPES, so the two cannot conflict.

The demo statement was not exercised against a live Dropbox Business account. That end-to-end confirmation was deferred from the first round under the commercial hold recorded on this task, and is a deliberate decision by Daniel rather than missing implementation.
